DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 14 s. 2022 Feb 23, 2022 Ms. DIWATA H. FETIZANAN Secretary Sangguniang Panlalawigan Province of Oriental Mindoro Provincial Capitol Complex Camilmil, Calapan, Oriental Mindoro Dear Ms. Fetizanan: This refers to your letter dated 03 December 2021 with attached Provincial Resolution No. 5651-2021 requesting from the Department a legal opinion on the following issues: I. Whether the provision of Local Budget Circular No. 63 issued on October 22, 1996 (Position Classification and Compensation of Barangay Officials and Personnel) [LBC 63-1996] that "the province and the, city or municipality where the barangay belongs cannot grant additional compensation to the barangay officials and employees in the form of honorarium or salary increase chargeable against either provincial, city, municipal or barangay funds" is still effective or superseded and amended by other subsequent issuances; and 2. What are the extent, nature and possible amount of compensation, honorarium or financial assistance that the [Provincial Government of Oriental Mindoro] may grant to qualified barangay personnel in the province, including the Barangay Tanod, Members of the Lupong Tagapamayapa, and Day Care Workers, under, form or chargeable to local or provincial funds. Based on our records, the said provision under Local Budget Circular No. 63 issued on October 22, 1996 (LBC 63-96) has not been superseded or amended by subsequent issuance/s. Verily, the same is still in effect unless later revoked or modified by the Department of Budget and Management. Nonetheless, the LBC 63-96 does not prohibit the adjustment of the rate of compensation and/or honorarium received by barangay officials pursuant to general salary adjustments or across the board increases authorized by the Office of the President. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In DBM Local Budget Circular No. 143, series of 2022 entitled "Implementation of the Third Tranche of the Modified Salary Schedule for Local Government Personnel Pursuant to Republic Act (RA) No. 11466", the following provision was included: Honoraria Adjustments for Barangay Officials and Employees 8.1 The maximum honoraria rates prescribed for barangay Officials and employees under LBC Nos. 63s and 137 may be adjusted following the salary schedule adopted by the municipality or city where the barangay belongs, subject to the PS limitation under Section 331(b) of R.A. No. 7160. 8.2 If barangay funds are not sufficient and sustainable to implement the honoraria rates authorized under Item 8.1, the Sangguniang Barangay may adjust the honoraria at lower rates but at a uniform percentage of the rates in Item 8.1 for all barangay officials and employees. As regards the second query, this Department respectfully submits that same has been addressed by this Department in a Letter dated 16 April 2020 (Letter) issued by the Undersecretary for Plans, Public Affairs, and Communications to the Department of Social Welfare and Development. A copy of the said letter is attached for your reference. For your guidance, the pertinent provisions of the Letter are reiterated as follows: Barangay Tanods Under Section 319 (16) of the Local Government Code [sic], the sanggunian of barangays [P]rovide for the organization of community brigades, barangay tanod, or community service units as may be necessary. Further, under- section 393 (a) of R.A. 7160, barangay tanods are entitled to receive honoraria, allowances, and other emoluments, viz: Section 393. Benefits of Barangay Officials. — (a) Barangay officials, including barangay tanods and members of the lupong tagapamayapa, shall receive honoraria, allowances, and such other emoluments as may be authorized by law or barangay, municipal or city ordinance in accordance with the provisions of this Code, but in no case shall it be less than One thousand pesos (Pl ,OOO.OO) per month for the punong barangay and Six hundred pesos (P600.OO) per month for the sangguniang barangay members, barangay treasurer, and barangay secretary: Provided, however, That the annual appropriations for personal services shall be subject to the budgetary limitations prescribed under Title Five, Book II of this Code; The ceiling for the grant Of the same should not exceed the minimum salary rate for SG I of the salary schedule being implemented by the city/municipality where the barangay belongs provided further that such compensation shall not exceed these of the lowest paid barangay officials pursuant to Local Budget Circular No. 63 (LBC '63') dated 22 October 1996, and Item 9.3.4.12.5 of the Manual on Position Compensation Classification Chapter 9. Notably, only barangay personnel who are paid salaries and whose positions are classified in accordance with RA 6758 and Issued appointments in accordance with the Civil Service law. rules and regulations pertaining thereto. may be entitled to the following benefits: personnel economic relief allowance (PERA); additional compensation; Year-End Bonus and cash gift: productivity incentive benefits; and other benefits accruing to regular employees. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Hence, barangay tanods are not entitled to receive other forms Of remunerations except honoraria, allowances, and other types of emoluments authorized by law or ordinance. Barangay Day Care Workers Barangay Day Care Workers belong to those positions other than the mandatory barangay officials which may be created h the barangay and may be compensated in the form of salary or honorarium at the discretion of the barangay government concemed. Thus, Barangay Day Care Workers are appointed by the barangay when a position for such is created by the unit. Under LBC 63, the ceiling for the honoraria of Barangay Daycare Workers should not exceed the salary rate for SG 6 of the Salary schedule being implemented by the city/municipality where the barangay belongs.. Similar to Tanods, Barangay Day Care Workers are not entitled to receive other forms of remunerations except honoraria, allowances, and other types of emoluments authorized by law or ordinance. " As stated above, lupon members and barangay tanods are compensated in the form of honoraria which shall not exceed SG I based on the salary schedule. Day Care Workers similarly receive honoraria which should not exceed SG 6. Unless otherwise provided by law, they are not entitled to PERA, additional compensation, year-end bonus, mid-year bonus, and other incentives accruing to regular employees of the barangay. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have sufficiently addressed your concerns. Thank you.
